entities.summary: Jehan-Ariste Paul Alain was a French organist, composer and soldier. Born into a family of musicians, he learned the organ from his father and a host of other teachers, becoming a composer at 18, and composing until the outbreak of the Second World War 10 years later. His compositional style was influenced by the musical language of the earlier Claude Debussy, as well as his interest in music, dance and philosophy of the far east. At the outbreak of the Second World War, Alain became a dispatch rider in the Eighth Motorised Armour Division of the French Army; he took part in the Battle of Saumur, in which he was killed.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jehan Alain's compositional style influenced French music during the interwar period, and his military service in World War II had a significant impact on the French Army's use of dispatch riders. His death at the Battle of Saumur resulted in the loss of a skilled organist and composer.
